💡 Key Takeaways
  • After backlash from sellers frustrated by Etsy’s new AI policies, which appeared to allow the tech giant to train AI on user artwork, Etsy has now clarified its stance.
  • In a note published on Monday, CEO Kruti Patel Goyal discussed recent tweaks to the company’s terms of service and admitted that her team “should’ve given you more context on what the updates meant for your creative content.”.
  • In a recent development, “Our recent terms patch was meant to reflect the evolving technologies we’re using to build better tools and experiences for sellers and the Etsy community,” Goyal wrote this week.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After backlash from sellers frustrated by Etsy’s new AI policies, which appeared to allow the tech giant to train AI on user artwork, Etsy has now clarified its stance.

In a note published on Monday, CEO Kruti Patel Goyal discussed recent tweaks to the company’s terms of service and admitted that her team “should’ve given you more context on what the updates meant for your creative content.”.

In a recent development, “Our recent terms patch was meant to reflect the evolving technologies we’re using to build better tools and experiences for sellers and the Etsy community,” Goyal wrote this week. “It was not meant to enable us to train AI models for the purpose of creating copycats of your items. We do not and will not do that.”.

Aaron Meshon, a longtime professional illustrator and Etsy seller, told Ars that even though the organization had dialed back its AI language somewhat, the changes were mere “sugar coating.”.

He remarked he still prepares on shutting down his 15-year-old Etsy store on December 1.

“I would say I’m losing 20 percent of my yearly income,” he remarked. “It’s a few mortgage payments.”.

He noted that Etsy’s announcement also seems to be rather tone-deaf, given that many retailers make a substantial portion of their annual revenue in the run-up to the end-of-year holiday season.

“This is the worst two-to-three weeks out of the year to do this, bar none,” he noted.

The fracas began earlier this month, when the tech giant first proposed new contractual language. The updated terms read:.

As a result, a slew of vendors pulled up stakes, with some saying they had “burned their Etsy shop to the ground” or that they “just killed our Etsy store after 13 years.”.

Etsy’s change is reminiscent of a recent dust-up involving Meta, where the tech giant had wanted to “require Meta Business account users to allow extensive AI training on external websites linked on Facebook.” Meta then indefinitely paused that move.

Last month, Etsy also told sellers that it would “set clearer restrictions on AI use,” despite the fact that AI-generated items remain for sale all over the site.

“Today, many active buyers say they can’t tell which items involve AI-generated content,” James Ossman, the manufacturer’s vice president of customer operations, wrote on October 22. “It’s become a top-three barrier to shopping more often on Etsy.”.

For years, Etsy has been notoriously poor at enforcing its own rules, not only regarding AI but also the official prohibitions on selling sex toys, pornography, and even purported witchcraft spells.

Latest Update: DR Congo demands answers over Ugandan general's threats

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (629 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba's social media posts have previously sparked diplomatic tensions.
  • The Democratic Republic of Congo has summoned Uganda's top diplomat in Kinshasa over social media posts by Uganda's military chief, Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba, who is also the president's son.
  • In a series of X posts, Gen Kainerugaba appeared to support a rebel takeover of Walikale, a mineral-rich territory in eastern DR Congo.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba's social media posts have previously sparked diplomatic tensions.

The Democratic Republic of Congo has summoned Uganda's top diplomat in Kinshasa over social media posts by Uganda's military chief, Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba, who is also the president's son.

In a series of X posts, Gen Kainerugaba appeared to support a rebel takeover of Walikale, a mineral-rich territory in eastern DR Congo. He insisted that Uganda's military involvement was purely driven by security concerns.

The DR Congo's foreign ministry summoned Uganda's envoy to explain the remarks, describing them as "particularly serious" and damaging to diplomatic relations.

The Ugandan government has yet to respond.

The diplomatic row comes despite close military ties between the neighbours.

Their forces have been conducting joint operations against the Islamic State-linked Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) in eastern DR Congo since 2021.

Uganda has also recently been involved in efforts to mediate between the Congolese government and an armed group led by former warlord Thomas Lubanga in Ituri province.

Arrested generals and a threatened VP: President's son fuels Ugandan succession fever.

The Ugandan general who lobs grenades on Twitter.

In his posts, Gen Kainerugaba accused the Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Rwanda (FDLR), an armed group operating in eastern DR Congo, of targeting members of the Bahima ethnic community.

The Bahema are a traditionally cattle-herding community mainly based in DR Congo's north-eastern Ituri province.

They have historical and cultural ties to the Bahima people of neighbouring Uganda.

He also threatened a rebel takeover of Walikale, in North Kivu province, while defending Uganda's military presence in DR Congo.

Walikale is rich in mineral resources , including some of the country's largest tin deposits and several major gold mines.

Gen Kainerugaba's X account, which had nearly 1.4 million followers, has since become inaccessible.

It is unclear whether he deactivated it, as he has done in the past, or whether the platform had suspended it.

During the same week he declared: "My tweets in Uganda are directives that must be obeyed.".

The posts followed reports that a DR Congo military aircraft had allegedly been shot down by rebels, with foreign mercenaries reportedly among those on board.

Gen Kainerugaba criticised the reported presence of foreign mercenaries in DR Congo.

"These remarks, which are particularly serious, have caused a major media incident and undermine the necessary restraint that must prevail in relations between sovereign states," the DR Congo foreign ministry said in a statement on Wednesday.

"The Congolese government expects the Republic of Uganda to clarify its official position and take the necessary measures to prevent such transgressions from recurring in the future".

The ministry added that DR Congo remained committed to regional peace and stability but would defend its dignity and institutions against "any form of provocation or interference".

It is not the first time Gen Kainerugaba's social media posts have strained relations between the two countries.

In February last year, he threatened to seize the eastern DR Congo city of Bunia, claiming that members of the Bahima ethnic community were being attacked.

In 2024, DR Congo also summoned Uganda's diplomatic representative after the general made threats against foreign mercenaries operating in eastern DR Congo.

The 52-year-old general, widely seen as a potential successor to his father Yoweri Museveni, has become known for his provocative social media posts.

In 2022, he sparked a diplomatic row with neighbouring Kenya after threatening to invade the country and capture its capital, Nairobi, prompting his father to apologise forn the remarks.

The proposed sale would include explicit conversations with children, officials say.

Sources indicate that character.AI is still drawing controversy and legal scrutiny even during its bankruptcy proceedings. A group of 42 attorneys general are trying to block the chatbot manufacturer from auctioning off people' chat histories and other sensitive information.

Industry observers note that but the auction for Character.AI won't actually safeguard customers' data at all, according to the state AGs. "Character.AI's plan to auction off its platform, including the IP addresses and private chats histories of its users — many of them children — with zero protection for those users is appalling," California Attorney General Rob Bonta stated in a statement. "If this sale goes through, users' sensitive data would go into the hands of a buyer even though Character.AI promised consumers that their data would not be sold.".

According to Bonta's office, the proposed sale includes chat histories, including conversations "in which AI characters drew children and adults into explicit sexual conversations." The buyer would also get access to chats in which consumers interacted with AI characters posing as physicians and therapists and discussed self harm, eating disorders, suicidal thoughts and other sensitive topics.

Industry observers note that the AGs have also raised concerns about the fact that only one anonymous bidder has been disclosed so far. That entity, called Smirks and Pangs Acquisition LLC, was formed "one day before Character.AI picked it as the base bid for the auction," and its source of funding hasn't been disclosed. "Nothing in the agreement restricts what the buyer may do with the data after closing, including selling it," the AGs say in a court filing.

The auction is right now scheduled for December 1. The AGs are asking the bankruptcy court to block the sale to Smirks and deny a "break-up fee" that would allow the company to collect $350,000 if Character.AI sells to another buyer. They're also asking for children's chatbot conversations and "sensitive" data to be barred from any potential sale.

It has been revealed that "Children and families who shared their most personal thoughts with Character.AI never imagined those conversations could be auctioned off to the highest bidder," Colorado Attorney General Phil Weiser noted in a statement. "A company's financial troubles do not give it the right to disregard its responsibility to protect consumers, especially children.

    Thirteen dead as mine disaster highlights illegal hunt for gold

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (983 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It's been three days since Rani last saw her father as he left for work on Monday.
    • Rais, 50, had been working as an illegal gold miner in Bogor, Indonesia's West Java province.
    • Sources indicate that authorities on Thursday confirmed that 13 people had died and their bodies were recovered from the site.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The flooded mine is in Bogor in West Java.

    It's been three days since Rani last saw her father as he left for work on Monday. Early on Tuesday, she received news that he was trapped underground.

    Rais, 50, had been working as an illegal gold miner in Bogor, Indonesia's West Java province. On Monday night, he and at least 25 other miners were digging in an open-pit mine about 100m (328ft) deep, when torrential rain caused a nearby river to overflow and flood the two shafts.

    Sources indicate that authorities on Thursday confirmed that 13 people had died and their bodies were recovered from the site. At least 13 more are thought to still be missing.

    Search-and-rescue operations are ongoing, with personnel using ropes to access the depths of the dark, narrow and slippery mine shafts, which are continually being flooded from below.

    Above ground, ambulances and medical personnel are ready and waiting to transport victims.

    "We are coordinating with all search and rescue personnel involved in the operation to monitor water conditions and assess access to the mine shaft," Desiana Kartika Bahari, head of the Jakarta Search and Rescue Office, remarked in a statement on Wednesday.

    "The depth of the shaft, narrow access and limited lighting are key considerations in determining the search strategy so that personnel can operate safely.".

    Rescuers have been working day and night to find survivors in the flooded mine shaft.

    Small-scale gold mining is banned in Indonesia, but remains widespread in rural parts of the mineral-rich archipelago.

    In a recent development, multiple studies show that over the past ten years the illegal industry has rapidly flourished, often in correlation with rising gold prices. In early 2026, those prices reached an all-time high â spurring a gold rush that prompted mine operators across the country to expand their operations.

    In a recent development, this included state-owned mining organization Aneka Tambang (Antam), which owns the business permit for the area in which this week's flooded mine is located. Antam have said the mine was not theirs and was operating without their authorisation.

    On Wednesday, while rescue operations there were underway, West Java Regional Police separately confirmed that they had uncovered 24 cases of illegal mining across the province between October and November alone.

    But Bisman Bakhtiar, Executive Director of the Center for Energy and Mining Law Studies, told the BBC earlier this year that the actual number of illegal mines in Indonesia is higher than the government's figures.

    "[The government figures are] what's been recorded. That means there must be more than that," he mentioned, noting that law enforcement operations have had little impact on the sector.

    "It's still very massive and very significant because this has been going on for a very long time.".

    Others allege that the illegal industry is underpinned by corruption.

    Laode M Syarif, former deputy chairman of the Corruption Eradication Committee, said that unofficial mining is difficult to eradicate because every illegal mine has "backing", usually from "police and military or high-ranking officials in local and provincial governments".

    "As long as these backers are not dealt with firmly, illegal mining will continue," he stated.

    In many cases, though, the allure of these mines is simple: they offer an economic lifeline to people with few other viable prospects.

    Despite the value of gold having dipped in recent months, countless illegal miners throughout Indonesia are still eagerly digging for paydirt.

    But the lack of regulation and poor construction in the pits also means accidents are relatively common â whether from landslides, floods, or exposure to hazardous gases, all of which have claimed lives in recent years.

    Relatives of the missing Bogor miners have been waiting near the site for news of their loved ones.

    Earlier this year, in the same area as this week's flooded mine, 11 illegal gold miners reportedly died after a carbon monoxide leak inside a shaft.

    Elsewhere, in West Sumatra, nine people were killed at an illegal gold mine in May after heavy rain triggered the collapse of a 30-metre cliff, burying 12 miners in total.

    There are numerous reports of other such incidents across the Indonesian archipelago. But the illegal nature of the small-scale gold mining sector obfuscates the true number of casualties.

    Even this week, when asked how many miners were in the pits in Bogor when they flooded, M Adam Hamdani, head of emergency and logistics at the Bogor Regency Regional Disaster Management Agency, remarked the total casualty figure "is still unclear".

    "Some say 20 people, others say 29 people," Hamdani told Indonesian news outlet Detik. "The problem is that no one reported it and no one wants to report it.".

    The Indonesian Ombudsman on Thursday urged law enforcement officials to conduct a thorough investigation of the incident and to address the larger systemic concern behind it.

    "This should be a momentum for all parties to resolve the [illegal gold mining] problem comprehensively, not just taking action after the incident or closing the holes discovered," said Abdul Ghoffar, a member of the Indonesian Ombudsman.

    Recent findings suggest that "We need to uncover the entire [illegal gold mining] chain," he continued. "We must not allow only the miners in the field to be seen and prosecuted, while those who control the activities, provide capital and facilities, store, and market the mined products remain untouched.

    "Law enforcement must target the actors and networks that keep this illegal activity going.".

    Recent findings suggest that as rescue operations continue and more bodies are recovered, the picture is becoming less murky. But even if there are survivors among those who remain missing, time may be running out.

    More than three days since the shafts flooded, the relatives of the anonymous men in the mines are desperately waiting to hear whether their loved ones survived.

    As she waits for news of her father, Rani says: "I hope he's found soon.".

    #140061. 7 gadgets that'll instantly upgrade your Thanksgiving feast

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Engadget ↗ Open Full Page

    7 gadgets that'll instantly upgrade your Thanksgiving feast

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1536 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • These tools will make turkey day just a little easier.
    • We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.
    • Thanksgiving is supposed to be a time for rest, relaxation and appreciating all the good things that have happened to you over the past year.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    These tools will make turkey day just a little easier.

    We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.

    Thanksgiving is supposed to be a time for rest, relaxation and appreciating all the good things that have happened to you over the past year. However, there's no denying that it's also a ton of work for whoever is in charge of preparing your Thanksgiving meal. Not only do you have to consider the cooking itself, there's all the other things that come with making a holiday feast like choosing the right recipes, gathering all the ingredients and scheduling which dishes need to be cooked at what time so everything is ready together. And all that doesn't even include managing anyone who feels like helping, which can turn into its own logistical matter.

    So to help smooth out the chaos that is holiday cooking, we've put together a collection of essential cooking gadgets that can save you time and take some of the stress out of preparing your Thanksgiving bounty.

    In a recent development, most people probably wouldn't consider a knife to be very techy, and for most blades that sentiment rings true. But on days like Thanksgiving where you're going to be doing a ton of chopping, cutting, slicing and more, it can't hurt to have a little extra help. And then there's the turkey, because it isn't going to carve itself. Furthermore, if you want your bird to look anything like it does in cooking videos with those neat, super clean slices, you're going to need a sharp tool to get there.

    For cooking nerds who like to geek out about the science of sharpness, one of my favorite knives on the market right now is the Seattle Ultrasonics C-200. In addition to just being a really nice knife featuring a three-layer san mai blade made out of Japanese AUS-10 steel, inside its handle there's a motor that vibrates the knife 30,000 times per second. While the oscillations are so small that you can't actually feel it shaking, those vibrations increased the knife's effective sharpness by up to 50 percent. It excels at delicate foods like tomatoes that often like to stick to the side of your blade, but also denser things like potatoes and meat, which obviously includes turkey. The C-200 even comes with an IP65 rating for dust and water resistance, so there's no worry about ruining its electronics with an errant splash. And if you opt for the wireless charging tile, you'll never have to worry about keeping its battery topped up. Granted, starting at $399, it certainly isn't cheap, but that price is very much in the same range as other premium chef knives from big name companies like Shun, Wusthoff and others.

    Alternatively, if you want a dedicated gadget for helping you carve a turkey, you can always turn to more traditional electric knives like those from Cusinart, NutriChef, Hamilton Beach and more. Admittedly, these types of knives aren't nearly as pretty as blades like the C200 and the need to plug them in makes them harder to use on an everyday basis. But if you want a relatively easy and affordable way to make serving your Thanksgiving turkey go a bit more smoothly, a classic electric knife is definitely worth a look.

    Even if you prefer side dishes like mashed potatoes, stuffing or a green bean casserole, there's no denying that the turkey is the star of Thanksgiving dinner. And if you want it to come out just right, you need a decent thermometer. Not having one is basically gambling that you get lucky with your timing and the bird turns out well. That said, there are a range of options, from simple digital sticks like the affordable ThermoPop 2 to fancy probe thermometers like the second-gen model from Combustion Inc.

    Industry observers note that basic options require a bit more work as you can't leave them in the bird while it's in the oven, whereas more expensive versions have wireless support that allows you to leave them inside the turkey as it cooks. Some options like those from Combustion Inc. even account for carry-over cooking, which is when the temperature of the food continues to rise even after you take it out of the oven. You just need to decide how much you want to spend and what kind of features you really want. One of my more affordable favorites is the Sense from Chef IQ, which offers a great balance between price and performance. Just don't be a fool and try to rely strictly on the little pop-out thermometers that sometimes come with the bird, as those aren't known for their accuracy or precision.

    A major concern during Thanksgiving is not having enough room in your oven for everything that needs to be baked or roasted. One easy solution to this is turning to an air fryer, which works almost exactly like the convection function on an oven, but in a smaller volume that's faster to heat and sometimes offers better air circulation. Another really nice thing about air fryers is that they can be quite affordable, with name brand models like the Instant Pot Vortex or the Ninja Air Fryer Pro, both of which are currently going for as little as $80.

    Upgrading to more expensive fryers like the Philips 3000 can give you more capacity, while even pricier options like the Wonder Oven Pro from Our Place have as many as eight different functions for things like baking, roasting, dehydrating, proofing and more. And perhaps the best thing is that when the holidays are over, you can easily move these into your pantry, closet or garage and reclaim some of your precious kitchen counter space.

    It has been revealed that A good digital scale falls in the same general camp as a decent thermometer and there isn't an experienced baker that would be caught dead without one. They're super easy to use and in my opinion, they are a staple of any well-equipped kitchen. You can just plop a mixing bowl on top, zero out the scale and then add ingredients in as needed while you get precise measurements, which can be especially critical for baked goods and confections. OXO makes a very nice and rather affordable digital scale that starts at around $65, but you can find cheaper options from well-known brands like KitchenAid for barely more than $20.

    A lot of people think blenders are big, bulky contraptions that make a ton of noise and take up too much room in your kitchen. And while the most powerful ones often are, they don't need to be, as there are affordable options that aren't much bigger than a teapot like these ones from Magic Bullet and Ninja. Regardless, they are great for making a post-dinner milkshake or a lovely fall-inspired soup (butternut squash anyone?).

    Industry observers note that alternatively, you can opt for an immersion blender (aka a hand blender), which can do much of the same functions as a big countertop model, but gives you even greater control and the ability to blend things directly on the stovetop using the pots you already own. This can make them better choices for whipping up sauces like hollandaise (which is delicious when poured over roasted asparagus), mayonnaise or even a classic cranberry sauce to go with your turkey. I prefer cordless options like those from KitchenAid as they have more than enough battery life to complete multiple dishes and the lack of a wire makes them super easy to use. But if your budget is tight, traditional cabled options are totally fine too and often a more affordable choice.

    Even for people like me who prefer to chop things by hand, a food processor can be an incredible time saver during the holidays. Not only do they make quick minces of veggies, they can also be used to grate cheese, shred things like potatoes (for an easy Thanksgiving hash), or whip up dips like salsa. Some options like the Cusinart Mini Food processor are stupendously cheap at under $30, while pricer models like the Ninja Professional Plus Food Processor come with a bunch of attachments to handle all sorts of dishes.

    Cooking food in a water bath might seem like an unnecessarily complex thing to do for the holidays, but it can actually save you time and effort. A good sous vide machine like those from Anova or Breville allow you to set an exact temperature and hold it there almost indefinitely. This allows you to cook things like meat with precision, so there's no worrying about if something is going to come out medium-rare or well-done.

    And even on Thanksgiving where turkey is the main protein, you can still use a sous vide machine to make dishes like superb rosemary mashed potatoes or luscious glazed carrots. Some models even come with Wi-Fi, so you can start and set them remotely using your phone. On top of that, all they need to function is an outlet, so a sous vide machine can be a great option for people with small kitchens or a limited number of burners on their stove.

    #140059. Breaking: Ladybird browser's first downloadable alpha is surprisingly capable

    📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (988 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Ars Technica ↗ Open Full Page

    Breaking: Ladybird browser's first downloadable alpha is surprisingly capable

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (988 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that note: At the time of writing, I was unaware of criticism directed at Ladybird creator Andreas Kling’s public statements.
    • Recent findings suggest that after four years of work to build a browser engine from scratch, the Ladybird project released its first downloadable alpha on November 23, offering prebuilt versions for macOS and Linux.
    • In a recent development, ladybird is most notable for what it isn’t: another browser fork.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that note: At the time of writing, I was unaware of criticism directed at Ladybird creator Andreas Kling’s public statements. Readers interested in this background can find further context in accounts by Kelson Vibber and Drew DeVault.

    Recent findings suggest that after four years of work to build a browser engine from scratch, the Ladybird project released its first downloadable alpha on November 23, offering prebuilt versions for macOS and Linux. Previously, curious consumers had to compile the browser themselves from its source. Now it’s an installable package with automatic updating.

    In a recent development, ladybird is most notable for what it isn’t: another browser fork. Where Chrome, Edge, Brave, and Opera all run on Google’s Blink engine, and Firefox depends on Gecko, Ladybird’s rendering engine and its LibJS JavaScript engine were written from scratch. “The engine is our own, built from the ground up, and not a fork,” project lead Andreas Kling wrote in Monday’s announcement. “The browser around it is modest, but functional.”.

    Nearly the entire modern web currently runs on three browser engines. There’s WebKit (Safari), Gecko (Firefox), and the biggest of them all, Blink (Chromium). Those limited options mean that web developers often end up optimizing sites for Chromium specifically, since that’s where the majority of traffic is, and as a result, the whole web platform tends to follow suit toward whatever the dominant engine supports.

    It has been revealed that an independent implementation of web standards has value not just by providing additional competition in the market, but because it can’t help but reveal places where sites depend on Chromium behaviors rather than published specifications. The fact that Ladybird exists isn’t likely to shift the market tides any time soon, but every upcoming browser engine increases the number of implementations that standards can be tested against, which can surface Chromium-specific assumptions and push the ecosystem toward the spec.

    In a recent development, the Ladybird project was borne out of Kling’s SerenityOS project, an attempt to develop a fresh independent OS from scratch, before splitting off as a separate project. Kling formed the Ladybird Browser Initiative, a 501(c)(3) nonprofit funded by sponsorships and donations. The project’s site highlights that there are no sponsored search engine deals supporting the project like many other popular browsers, and sponsoring entities have no say in the project roadmap.

    According to recent reports, the Ladybird alpha is a rolling release channel that updates automatically, and the downloadable package is a huge step to getting the browser onto the PCs of everyday users. “Ladybird improves quickly, and until now you had to build it from source to see that,” Kling wrote. Though the browser began as C++, in keeping with the ethos of SerenityOS, the project has since started shifting toward Rust, starting with its JavaScript engine.

    Recent findings suggest that while it’s exciting to have a new engine option for browsing, the project leader notes that this is still a very early release. The browser build contains a built-in tool for reporting any websites that fail to render or crash the browser. Kling writes, “We want security nerds to hack it! A new browser gets hacked, over and over, and that’s part of the process, so we make no promises about security today.”.

    Microsoft users are still out in the cold on this one for now. The project states that future support for Windows is planned, but it’s macOS and Linux only for now.

    I tested the Ladybird alpha version 2026.47.8 on my AceMagic W1 mini PC AMD Ryzen 7 8745HS with 16GB DDR5 and running Fedora Linux 44 with the upcoming KDE Plasma 6.8.3, and the most surprising thing about the alpha build was how little it feels like alpha software.

    The browser seemed to handle most anything I threw at it without glitch. Day-to-day tabbed browsing mechanics felt snappy and normal. A 50MB test video file downloaded quickly and smoothly. With a dozen tabs open, switching between them was instant, and the browser felt responsive throughout. Options menus were surprisingly fleshed out for a build this young.

    Google Maps loaded instantly, located me, and handled everything I threw at it: adding and removing layers, zooming out from the Midwest, and dropping into Street View in Alberta, Canada in around three seconds. Everything rendered fast enough that my mini PC’s fan spun up noticeably. GitHub’s site, including repository navigation, worked without a hitch. So did YouTube and the news sites I tried.

    Sources indicate that I could stall the browser, but it took some effort. With about 10 tabs open, I was streaming a 4K test video file from my personal Jellyfin server. Everything worked fine at first, but after skipping around in the file over and over again, the browser eventually got stuck. Mind you, this is an alpha build that I was trying to trip up, not a representation of something inherently broken.

    Industry observers note that after spending an evening with Ladybird, I can say that while it won’t be replacing Firefox for me anytime soon, I was genuinely impressed that a scratch-made engine could perform this well in such an early state. Most fresh browser projects are forks of something that already exists. Ladybird is the rare exception, an engine written from nothing, and the alpha runs well enough that if you have a Mac or Linux PC handy, it’s worth downloading a build and poking around yourself. Just remember Kling’s warning: This is nowhere near trustworthy enough to make your daily driver, yet.

    What the alpha demonstrates is that a small team of independent developers, funded by donations, has built a browser engine from scratch that handles real web browsing without a fuss. That it works this well this soon, using no existing engine code, is an achievement. I thought I was a Firefox loyalist, but I’ll be keeping an eye on where this one goes.

    Can you play GTA 6 from an external hard drive on PS5 or Xbox Series X/S?

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (300 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Engadget

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Rockstar’s behemoth takes up a lot of storage space.
    • It has been revealed that grand Theft Auto 6 is the biggest game of the year by some distance, having racked up $3.79 billion in pre-orders and day-one sales.
    • There will be many other folks who want to play the game and haven't had a chance to jump in yet.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Rockstar’s behemoth takes up a lot of storage space.

    It has been revealed that grand Theft Auto 6 is the biggest game of the year by some distance, having racked up $3.79 billion in pre-orders and day-one sales. On PlayStation 5 alone, more than 39 million unique players took control of dual protagonists Jason and Lucia on opening weekend, making it the biggest game debut in the 32-year history of PlayStation.

    There will be many other folks who want to play the game and haven't had a chance to jump in yet. One thing they should note is that, with a hefty install size, GTA 6 will take up a significant chunk of their PS5 or Xbox Series X/S storage space.

    You might be wondering whether you can install GTA 6 on an external hard drive to avoid having to delete other games and data from your console. You can move GTA 6 to your external storage when you're not playing it. However, to run the game locally, you'll need to have it installed on your system's built-in storage, an SDD you've installed in your PS5 or a compatible NVMe expansion card that's plugged into your Xbox.

    According to recent reports, as with many other recent games, GTA 6 needs to take advantage of the fast-loading capabilities of the PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. The consoles are unable to load data for these titles promptly enough from an external hard drive over a USB connection. For the same reason, disc-based PS5 and Xbox Series X games are installed onto system storage before you can play them. The PS5 can run PS4 games from external storage, though. Likewise, an Xbox Series X/S can run older Xbox One and Xbox 360 titles directly from an external hard drive.

    A Hamas political official and his wife were among eight Palestinians killed in three Israeli air strikes across the Gaza Strip on Thursday.

    Local sources told the BBC a residential apartment in Deir al-Balah was targeted at dawn, killing Khaled Abu Nada - the deputy education minister - and his wife, Abeer Mohammed Ismail Abu Nada.

    A Hamas Civil Defence spokesman stated that rescue teams and medical personnel had transferred eight bodies to Al-Aqsa Hospital in central Gaza and Al-Shifa Hospital in Gaza City.

    In a joint statement, Israel's prime minister and defence minister stated the operation was "part of a series of targeted killings" against Hamas officials.

    Thursday's strikes also reportedly killed three Palestinians on al-Nafaq Street, east of Gaza City. Their identities have not yet been established, eyewitnesses remarked.

    In a separate strike on Shati refugee camp, west of Gaza City, three Palestinians working for Hamas's security services were killed. They were identified as Yasser al-Lahham, Iyad Ahmed and Ibrahim al-Mashal.

    Khaled Abu Nada and his wife Abeer Mohammed Ismail Abu Nada were killed in the air strike.

    In a post X, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu confirmed the death of Khaled Abu Nada and noted about 80 Hamas officials have been killed in the last month.

    "No one in Hamas's leadership will succeed in evading us," he remarked, adding that the military would "continue to pursue our enemies and protect the security of Israeli civilians".

    The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) remarked it had carried out a strike on a "senior" Hamas operative, and would provide further details later.

    The attacks came a day after Mohammed Abu al-Ouf, 47, the head of Hamas's internal security service in northern Gaza, his wife and their two teenage daughters were killed in Israeli air strike on their apartment in Shati refugee camp in Gaza City.

    On Tuesday, the overall commander of Hamas's internal security service was among 10 Palestinians reportedly killed in Israeli strikes.

    Violence has continued in Gaza since Israel and Hamas agreed to a US-brokered ceasefire in October last year. Israeli strikes take place almost daily in areas under Hamas's control, which are home to 2.1 million people, most of them displaced.

    At least 1,705 people have been killed in Gaza over the past 13 months, according to the territory's Hamas-run health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the UN.

    Israel states six of its soldiers have been killed in Gaza during the same period.

    The Gaza war was triggered by the Hamas-led attack on southern Israel on 7 October 2023, when about 1,200 people were killed and 251 others were taken hostage.

    Since then, more than 74,772 people have been killed in Israeli attacks in Gaza, the health ministry states.

While pursuing the freedom fighter through hills and valleys in the homeland of the Naga people, colonial officers also seized some of her most treasured possessions.

    They were sent to the University of Oxford’s Pitt Rivers Museum and kept in storage. Now, for the first time, the museum is exhibiting the collection of 27 items, including a basket of Gaidinliu’s notebooks believed to contain her prophetic visions as the leader of a Naga Indigenous religion, clothes, bracelets and amulets.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Black Friday sales can save you money on the latest from Apple, Google and more.

    We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.

    Black Friday isn't quite the major sales event it used to be now that you can get deals multiple times a year through events like Amazon Prime Day, but if you're looking to save this holiday season, there are still some great options.

    Multiple gadgets from Engadget's Best of 2026 list are already on sale, including Samsung's flagship foldable smartphone and Apple's ultra-popular (and cute) entry-level laptop. Online retailers like Amazon seem to offer the steepest discounts, but buying directly from the manufacturer can also net you extra savings, particularly if you have a device you want to trade in. If you don't see what you want on sale now, worry not: New deals will continue to pop up throughout Thanksgiving and Black Friday. In the meantime, here's a selection of what you can save on now.

    Apple has had a big year of product releases, both in terms of wholly new product categories and old standbys it's finally shown some love. The organization is running its own Black Friday sale on its website through November 30, which can net you Apple gift cards ranging from $25 to $300 depending on the product you purchase, but you can also find some excellent deals on Amazon.

    Industry observers note that the colorful latest MacBook Neo, Apple's first computer powered by an iPhone chip (the A18 Pro) and its first relatively budget-friendly laptop, is on sale at Amazon for $649, $50 off its normal $699 starting price. The Neo made a big splash when it launched in March because it offered some of the premium benefits of Apple's more expensive computers at an affordable $599, a price Apple unfortunately raised to $699 in June due to the high cost of memory and storage. This discount helps recapture some of that original magic.

    If you'd prefer something more powerful, you can also opt for the new M5 MacBook Air, which is on sale on Amazon for $1,049, $250 off its normal $1,299 price. The new M5 chip is the main upgrade this year, and it offers more than enough power for basic work, with extra headroom for AI tools and light gaming.

    Arguably the best Apple deals so far, though, are the current discounts on the AirPods Pro 3 and the Apple Watch Series 12. You can purchase Apple's high-end wireless earbuds for just $149 on Amazon, a 40 percent discount on the usual $249 Apple charges. Meanwhile, Apple's latest smartwatch — which features a redesigned health sensor — is going for $299 on Amazon, $100 off its normal $399 price.

    Like Apple, Google is offering some exclusive deals on its website if you're interested in saving on accessories or getting an even better deal on a trade-in. The bulk of the company's discounts on smartphones and smartwatches are being reflected across retailers, though.

    According to recent reports, for example, both the Pixel 11 and Pixel 11 Pro are on sale on Amazon. The base Pixel 11, which comes in new colors, includes more storage and has a collection of AI-powered camera features, is on sale on Amazon for $699, over 20 percent off its normal $899 starting price. You can also get the Pixel 11 Pro, Google's higher-end model with its new HiLight customizable notification light, for $749 on Amazon, a $350 discount on its usual $1,099 starting price.

    If you've already got an Android phone and are looking for a good smartwatch, you can get a Pixel Watch 5, Google's latest smartwatch, on sale on Amazon for $330, $100 off its $430 starting price. The new smartwatch offers easy access to Gemini, improved GPS tracking for outdoor workouts and new gestures for controlling the watch without using the touchscreen.

    Recent findings suggest that while Apple's first foldable, the iPhone Duo, is the hot commodity heading into the holiday season, it doesn't yet have an easy-to-snag Black Friday deal. You can get Engadget's favorite foldable of the year for a healthy discount, though.The Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 features a latest, more passport-shaped form factor and one of the company's best anti-glare displays. It's also available on Amazon for $1,550, a still eye-popping price, but cheaper than the $1,900 Samsung usually charges. If you're on Android and Duo-curious, the Z Fold 8 is the better foldable anyway.

    According to recent reports, for anyone all-in on Gemini and Google's Pixel ecosystem, the less beloved but still competently made Pixel 11 Pro Fold is on sale on Amazon for $1,649. That's a $250 discount on what's usually a $1,899 foldable, and you still get Google's polished take on Android and extensive software support.

    If you're building out a home office or setting up your first PC gaming rig, you'll want a monitor you're willing to stare at for hours on end. The Alienware 39 5K not only offers ample screen real estate with its 39-inch, ever-so-slightly curved display, but also a wonderfully bright and vivid OLED panel that can switch between 5K 165Hz and 1080p+ 330Hz modes with a button push.

    According to recent reports, the monitor is on sale directly through Dell's website for $1,000, $100 off what Dell normally charges. If you want the best experience for gaming and staring at Microsoft Word, it's hard to go wrong with the Alienware 39 5K.

    Amazon and Meta reportedly in talks to lift blockade on AI agent Muse

    ⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Amazon may be having a change of heart about Meta’s AI agent, Muse.
    • The talks would mark a significant reversal from just two months ago, when Muse users discovered they were unable to purchase products on Amazon and instead received an error message when attempting to check out.
    • Industry observers note that according to a Wednesday report by Fortune, citing people familiar with the discussions, Amazon and Meta have held multiple rounds of talks about the matter.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Amazon may be having a change of heart about Meta’s AI agent, Muse. The two tech giants are reportedly discussing a potential deal that would allow Meta’s popular AI agent to connect directly to Amazon’s store.

    The talks would mark a significant reversal from just two months ago, when Muse users discovered they were unable to purchase products on Amazon and instead received an error message when attempting to check out.

    Industry observers note that according to a Wednesday report by Fortune, citing people familiar with the discussions, Amazon and Meta have held multiple rounds of talks about the matter. Two key concerns remain under negotiation: how search results would be presented and how advertising would be handled under a potential agreement.

    Sources indicate that one of Amazon’s biggest concerns is how third-party shopping agents like Muse could affect its advertising business. In October, Amazon CEO Andy Jassy argued that few customers were making purchases through outside shopping agents.

    In a recent development, amazon may also have been waiting for Muse to mature before agreeing to integrate it with its marketplace. If Muse places the wrong order or creates a problem with a purchase, Amazon could ultimately be left dealing with frustrated customers and unhappy sellers.

    Fortune reported that executives are concerned that third-party shopping agents could weaken Amazon’s direct relationship with consumers, according to people familiar with the matter.

    Any potential agreement between Amazon and Meta would reportedly require approval from both companies’ CEOs, Fortune also reported.

    Meta and Amazon have not yet responded to TechCrunch’s requests for comment.

    Newly introduced York governor Kathy Hochul has signed into law a five-year ban on the sale of AI chatbot toys, including dolls and robots that use the internet to converse with children. The new law comes with some teeth, including steep daily fines for each violation enforced by the state's attorney general.

    In a recent development, "Parents shopping for gifts for the holidays or any other occasion should not have to worry that dangerous chatbots disguised as toys could expose their children to inappropriate conversations, manipulate their feelings or put their privacy at risk," Hochul stated in a statement. Calling herself New York's first "mom governor," Hochul said the new measure was "deeply personal.".

    The governor's press release cited the US Public Interest Research Group Education Fund (PIRG), that tested chatbot toys marketed to children aged three to 12. Some of the toys talked about sexually explicit subjects and provided advice that could create a fire hazard in homes. The toys had few or zero parental controls and the longer the conversation, the more safety limits weakened. Some toys could even record a child's voice or scan their face.

    "AI chatbots in children's toys are exposing young people to inappropriate content and putting their mental health at risk," said New York attorney general Letitia James.

    In a recent development, violators face civil penalties up to $15,000 per day for each violation, according to the governor's office. James added that her branch would "not hesitate to enforce this law and other measures to stop AI systems from doing harm. We won't allow our children's health to become the collateral damage of massive tech.".

    According to recent reports, hochul and Upcoming York State legislators recently enacted another law called "AI Chatbot Restrictions for Minors," prohibiting unsafe chatbot features for children under 18, with civil penalties of up to $25,000 per infraction. Hochul also signed an executive order this summer, issuing a one-year ban data centers using 50MW or more.

    Anti-AI measures were a politically popular during US midterm elections, as Americans voted to restrict the country's data center boom. Data centers were the subject of 45 ballot measures in 10 states and 39 measures were passed to restrict the facilities in some form.

    Recent findings suggest that in a statement, Amazon said the products it sells must follow US laws. "We require all products sold by third-party sellers in our store to comply with applicable laws and regulations," Amazon told NBC News. "Amazon is committed to the safety of children and families. We support efforts across the industry and government to put appropriate guardrails in place as this technology develops." However, the retail giant sells some 12 million different toys in the US (as of 2023), so complying with the NY AI chatbot law could be a tall order.

    #140041. Tech Report: The FCC has authorized SpaceX to deploy 1 million satellites

    Tech Report: The FCC has authorized SpaceX to deploy 1 million satellites

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (660 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In an extraordinary decision, the Federal Communications Commission on Wednesday granted SpaceX conditional authorization to deploy a constellation of up to 1 million Starmind satellites designed to serve as orbital data centers.
    • If fully deployed, this constellation would increase the number of satellites in orbit by roughly 50-fold.
    • Sources indicate that “The United States is moving decisively to ensure that this breakthrough technology creates opportunity, drives investment, and delivers lasting benefits for the American people,” FCC Chairman Brendan Carr said in a statement on Wednesday.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In an extraordinary decision, the Federal Communications Commission on Wednesday granted SpaceX conditional authorization to deploy a constellation of up to 1 million Starmind satellites designed to serve as orbital data centers.

    If fully deployed, this constellation would increase the number of satellites in orbit by roughly 50-fold.

    Sources indicate that “The United States is moving decisively to ensure that this breakthrough technology creates opportunity, drives investment, and delivers lasting benefits for the American people,” FCC Chairman Brendan Carr said in a statement on Wednesday. “This action opens a bold newly introduced frontier for the computing infrastructure needed to power America’s leadership and growth.”.

    The decision, announced a day before the Thanksgiving holiday in the United States, represents a major regulatory victory for SpaceX and its founder, Elon Musk, who has allied himself with the Trump administration.

    Sources indicate that this announcement clears a major hurdle to deploying data centers in space, although it does not establish that orbital data centers are technically or economically viable. Nevertheless, the FCC authorization appears designed to give the company wide latitude as it works through these remaining issues.

    Recent findings suggest that for example, SpaceX has seven years to deploy a single operational Starmind satellite under the order. SpaceX has until November 2035 to deploy 100,000 operational satellites, and November 2040 for the full constellation. SpaceX, therefore, has a 14-year regulatory runway to deploy the most ambitious industrial project ever approved for spaceflight.

    Sources indicate that the authorization includes some conditional aspects. SpaceX has proposed operating in six orbits, ranging from 550 km to about 1,000 km. The organization sought a waiver from FCC rules to allow satellites above 600 km to be disposed of into “Earth disposal orbits or heliocentric orbits.” That is, instead of burning them up in Earth’s atmosphere, SpaceX wants the flexibility to move retired satellites into other orbits around Earth, or potentially into orbit around the Sun.

    The FCC did not grant this waiver request “because SpaceX has not provided sufficient information for the Commission to determine whether its alternative disposal methods are compliant with the Commission’s requirements.” The company will need to obtain a waiver before deploying any Starmind satellites that are not intended to be disposed of via atmospheric reentry.

    However, in other ways the FCC appears to have been incredibly lenient with SpaceX. This is particularly the case with environmental concerns raised by numerous parties that commented on SpaceX’s application to the FCC.

    Half a dozen organizations, such as the Secure World Foundation and American Astronomical Society, raised concerns about deploying so many satellites into orbit, citing collision risks, orbital debris, atmospheric pollution from so many satellite reentries, impacts on astronomical observations, and more. The FCC also received approximately 1,500 public comments concerning SpaceX’s application.

    According to recent reports, some of these environmental issues, the FCC remarked, lay beyond the scope of its review. For example, on concerns about the environmental implications of thousands or potentially tens of thousands of rocket debuts, the FCC said, “Potential concerns related to the emissions of rocket launches and the subsequent impacts on the human environment as an indirect result of the Starmind system are outside of the Commission’s purview.”.

    The FCC also rejected calls for further environmental scrutiny of pollution from satellite reentries, including concerns about aluminum oxides and their potential effects on the ozone layer. “Other concerns, including impacts on the atmosphere caused by satellites burning up on re-entry, remain speculative and not supported in the record,” the FCC authorization states.

    In a recent development, as part of its decision, the FCC cited a significant policy change adopted in October, when the agency concluded that space-based activities generally fall outside its obligations under the National Environmental Policy Act. The FCC reasoned that as these activities occur beyond US territory, they don’t constitute federal actions requiring environmental review. As a result, the agency declined to conduct a comprehensive environmental assessment of SpaceX’s Starmind constellation.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that "My time as president is coming to an end, and that is why it was important to me to travel to Africa one more time — to the continent that is particularly close to my heart," said Frank-Walter Steinmeier during his final official trip to Africa.
    • "For me personally, things have come full circle today," the president added during his opening remarks at the German-African Business Summit in Ghana.
    • This week, in addition to Ghana, he visited Cote d'Ivoire and Kenya with a business delegation from Germany.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that "My time as president is coming to an end, and that is why it was important to me to travel to Africa one more time — to the continent that is particularly close to my heart," said Frank-Walter Steinmeier during his final official trip to Africa. Over the course of 20 years, as president and before that as foreign minister, the veteran politician has made 30 trips to African countries.

    "For me personally, things have come full circle today," the president added during his opening remarks at the German-African Business Summit in Ghana. He was alluding to the first German-African business summit in Berlin in 2015, which Steinmeier opened while he was still foreign minister in the administration of former Chancellor Angela Merkel.

    This week, in addition to Ghana, he visited Cote d'Ivoire and Kenya with a business delegation from Germany.

    A lot has happened since 2015, Steinmeier stated. And yet: "We are still far from where we could be." Addressing Germany's business community, he said, "Be curious, take risks.".

    Sources indicate that as the applause rang out after the speech, Jude Numfor, who works for the energy tech giant REI in Cameroon, smiled. He too sees German companies as too risk-averse.

    "When the Chinese come, they say 'let's do it,' and the Germans say 'let's prepare it'," he told DW.

    Recent findings suggest that meanwhile, Africa's economy is growing rapidly. German-African foreign trade rose by 10.5% in 2025 to €63.4 billion ($69.4 billion). Africa's trade with the Asia-Pacific region is growing more slowly, but the absolute figures are also significantly higher.

    This reveals there is a great deal of potential in Africa's markets — especially in light of the emerging African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), which encompasses most of the continent.

    When it comes to direct investment, German companies are more hesitant than others — a trend observed not only by Numfor: China, Turkey and the Gulf states are willing to take on more risk and are pushing into these markets.

    The Chinese, in particular, are offering large loans to build key rail lines and ports, and they are buying up mines and raw materials in Africa. But since they usually bring their own low-wage labor force with them, China's investments often create few local jobs.

    Recent findings suggest that but such jobs would be the linchpin of Africa's future. In Kenya alone, 1 million young people enter the labor market each year; in Nigeria, the number is even higher, and some experts therefore anticipate even more irregular migration to Europe in the coming years.

    Germany has said there is a need for action: It supports vocational training in Africa and, for several years now, has also been allowing skilled workers to emigrate to Germany from Africa.

    To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

    Sources indicate that during his trip, Steinmeier also visited educational institutions such as the vocational school for mechanics and industrial maintenance in Abidjan, Cote d'Ivoire. In Kenya, he spoke with President William Ruto about the implications of the 2024 bilateral migration and mobility partnership and more opportunities for language and vocational training.

    Recent findings suggest that there are now around 9,500 Kenyans working in Germany, and nearly 1,300 in vocational training. "We want to open up opportunities for young people and create regular, fair and orderly pathways for labor and skilled worker migration," Steinmeier mentioned in Nairobi.

    Vocational training is said to be most effective where businesses and factories are being established.

    "A very favorable window of opportunity for investment is at the moment opening up in Africa," noted Fritz Audebert, CEO of ICUnet, a manufacturer that advises German firms on investment projects worldwide. "We've noticed a shift over the past two years or so, driven in part by geopolitical changes, the complicated situation in China, and most recently the war in Iran.".

    Sources indicate that "More and more companies are beginning to understand this," Audebert added. "While there are reservations, we're seeing a similar sentiment to that regarding India." What's new is that small and medium-sized enterprises from Germany are also showing interest in Africa.

    In a recent development, during the trip, Audebert was particularly impressed by Cote d'Ivoire, as he said, "because of the ministers' high level of expertise." The country is the world's largest cocoa exporter and possesses vital raw materials. "You can work well with this potential," he said.

    Members of the business delegation accompanying Steinmeier also agreed that the German automotive industry must focus more on the African market.

    "The middle class is growing in cities, and with it, the demand for mobility," stated Audebert.

    To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

    Sources indicate that markus Thill, president of Bosch Africa, confirms there is a considerable market for simple, gas- and diesel-driven cars. "Based on the auto industry's experience, we know that households worldwide with an annual income of €10,000 or more can afford a newly introduced car," remarked Thill. This would mean that potentially 5-10 million new cars per year could be built and sold in Africa.

    Instead, "we export millions of old used cars to Africa that would no longer be eligible for registration in Europe," he mentioned.

    Even though the focus of the trip was on the economy, "we shouldn't limit our view to that," Steinmeier noted at the end of his trip. Germany maintains a reliable political partnership with Cote d'Ivoire, Ghana and Kenya.

    "These are three countries with which we cooperate closely on the international stage, and in that sense, visiting them now was the right and deliberate choice," he stated.

    When asked to take stock of his 30 trips to African countries undertaken during his political career, Steinmeier said: "There is not one Africa, but many, and there are also very different, uneven developments there." This fact, he concluded, needs to be "communicated even more effectively" in Germany.

    Watch: Fire and smoke billows out of refinery owned by energy organization Bangchak Corporation.

    Nine people have been injured after an explosion at an oil refinery in Bangkok, authorities have mentioned.

    Three of them are in critical condition, according to news agency AFP, which noted the local hospital had revised its earlier assessment of four.

    A fire broke out after the blast at the Phra Khanong facility run by energy giant Bangchak Corporation in the east of Thailand's capital at around 14:45 (07:45 GMT).

    The tech giant said the fire was brought under control and put out within 30 minutes, adding that the cause of the incident was being investigated.

    Black smoke could be seen across Bangkok's skyline after the blast, as local officials told residents to leave the area.

    An alert sent to mobile phones by Bangkok authorities confirmed that the fire was under control, but urged people to avoid the area.

    Eyewitnesses shared video clips on social media of flames and smoke rising above the refinery.

    On a visit to the scene, Thailand's energy minister Akanat Promphan remarked it appeared the impact of the explosion was limited because the fire started in a distillation tower about 100m (330ft) from where oil was being stored.

    He said the incident was concerning as the refinery was in a residential area and the government was suspending production until it could be confident that operations would resume without any issues.

    Bangchak Corporation said air quality monitoring in the immediate area around the refinery was within normal ranges.

    It confirmed that production at the site, which can process up to 120,000 barrels of oil a day had been shut down. The manufacturer has a second refinery in Chonburi province, about 50 miles (80km) from Bangkok, handling a daily capacity of about 180,000 barrels.

    An explosion occurred at the Bangkok refinery in July 2012, sparking a fire but no reported injuries.

    Todoist confirms 6% of customers’ details were stolen in data breach

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Task management app Todoist mentioned on Tuesday that a hacker gained access to its production systems and stole customer data, including email IDs, password hashes, and account creation dates.
    • In a recent development, todoist remarked the attacker used stolen credentials to access the firm’s version control system and source code between November 22 and 23.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Task management app Todoist mentioned on Tuesday that a hacker gained access to its production systems and stole customer data, including email IDs, password hashes, and account creation dates. The organization said around 6% of its customers were affected and blamed stolen credentials for the breach.

    In a recent development, todoist remarked the attacker used stolen credentials to access the firm’s version control system and source code between November 22 and 23. The hacker then changed employee access controls and reached the app’s cloud infrastructure via an employee’s work account.

    Industry observers note that the hacker downloaded credentials of early Todoist owners whose passwords were stored using an older hashing method, but didn’t change any source code, the tech giant said. Todoist said it has blocked the attack path and reset passwords as a mitigation step, as well as disabled the Todoist for Outlook email add-on.

    For a small number of people, about 0.001% of its userbase, the hacker also searched through tasks, comments, and attachment names to look for credentials for other services, like API keys and access tokens.

    The hacker also pulled Todoist API tokens and Slack integration tokens, and looked for emails, addresses, and attachment file names through the Todoist for Outlook extension if it was connected to accounts and had permission to read emails.

    The organization said it has sent a notice to those affected and asked them to reset their credentials and change their login details in other places with the same password. The company is asking users to also upgrade API tokens, reconnect integrations, and revoke or replace any access keys, recovery phrases, or credentials they had stored in Todoist comments.

    Todoist noted it has also reset its internal access structure and how remote command execution works in its cloud environment to prevent such incidents in the future.

    Todoist’s founder and CEO Amir Salihefendić apologized to users about the incident on X, and stated the company will take a closer look at why it happened.

    According to recent reports, the to-do app’s data breach is the latest in a burgeoning list of data breaches in which hackers use stolen credentials to access data and systems at enterprises. So far this year, we’ve seen several companies fall victim to this form of attack, including Uber and Klue.

    • Elon Musk's Neuralink has received FDA permission to launch the first "pivotal" trial for its implantable LINK brain-computer interface, the manufacturer confirmed.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The study will evaluate the efficacity and safety of the organization’s LINK device.

    Elon Musk's Neuralink has received FDA permission to launch the first "pivotal" trial for its implantable LINK brain-computer interface, the manufacturer confirmed. The study represents a more advanced step in the company's efforts to develop a brain implant that allows people with paralysis to control devices using their brain alone. It will be open to a limited number of patients with ALS (amyotrophic lateral sclerosis), a progressive neurodegenerative disorder that damages nerve cells controlling voluntary muscle movement.

    Industry observers note that "We've received FDA approval to launch LINK, the first pivotal trial for an implantable brain-computer interface in the US," Neuralink declared on X. "This builds off of our work with 30+ participants with Neuralink to date.".

    It has been revealed that neuralink hit a milestone last year when the company revealed that its first participant with ALS named Bradford Smith was able to communicate using brain signals alone. "Neuralink has given me freedom, hope, and faster communication. ... It has improved my life so much. I'm so happy to be involved in something big that will help many people," Smith said at the time.

    According to recent reports, we've received FDA approval to launch LINK, the first pivotal trial for an implantable brain-computer interface in the US. This builds off of our work with 30+ participants with Neuralink to date.

    Those with ALS may be eligible. To learn more:https://t.co/dWhb5N4GdR pic.twitter.com/Vor7iXXCBA.

    — Neuralink (@neuralink) November 25, 2026.

    The FDA authorization was granted on an experimental basis, but it's a key step forward for Neuralink's LINK brain-implant system. The study will evaluate the ability of patients to control digital devices through thought, "with a focus on functional outcomes that improve independence in daily life," Neuralink wrote. It will also assess the system's long-term safety and reliability.

    WIth Neuralink's latest system, the firm's N1 implant is surgically placed in the skull, then the company uses its R1 robot to insert flexible electrodes into the brain. Neural activity from the brain associated with movement is then interpreted by software, which translates signals into commands for controlling computers or digital devices. The technology is designed to help patients communicate with the outside world, with the eventual goal to let them operate devices without keyboards or other physical controls.

    Sources indicate that neuralink remarked patients with ALS may be eligible for the LINK trial, but it didn't specify other requirements or the number of participants. It now has approval recruit participants, then conduct the study under an approved clinical protocol. If the technology proves to be safe, the trial may allow Neuralink to apply for more advanced trials and eventually release LINK onto the market.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Watch: Taylor on the 'overwhelming reaction' to Duran Duran's music.
    • Simon Le Bon, Sir Rod Stewart and Gary Kemp are among the pop stars who have paid tribute to Duran Duran guitarist Andy Taylor following his death at the age of 65.
    • Taylor co-wrote some of the group's biggest hits including Save A Prayer, Rio and Girls On Film.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Watch: Taylor on the 'overwhelming reaction' to Duran Duran's music.

    Simon Le Bon, Sir Rod Stewart and Gary Kemp are among the pop stars who have paid tribute to Duran Duran guitarist Andy Taylor following his death at the age of 65.

    Taylor co-wrote some of the group's biggest hits including Save A Prayer, Rio and Girls On Film.

    Le Bon and his bandmates paid tribute, saying "he brought an indelible fire and swagger to our music", while Sir Rod remembered his "dear pal" and Spandau Ballet's Kemp called him "a great player who set the tone for the 80s".

    Taylor's wife Tracey called him "the rock of our family", adding: "We will miss him every single day." He died after "a long and courageous battle with prostate cancer", Duran Duran said in a statement on Wednesday.

    Andy Taylor: Duran Duran's livewire guitarist who was a Wild Boy on stage and off.

    He died "peacefully at home, surrounded by his family, on Monday 23rd November", a statement said.

    Paying tribute, his Duran Duran bandmates said: "From the moment he arrived in Birmingham from the North East with a guitar and an unshakeable belief in what we could become, he brought an indelible fire and swagger to our music.

    "His playing drove the songs that took us around the world, and with a dry wit that was matched only by his wonderfully unsentimental, no-nonsense outlook on life he kept us grounded and gave the band its edge through the extraordinary years that followed.".

    They said their thoughts were with his wife, children and grandson.

    Le Bon stated there was a "a massive Andy Taylor shaped hole in my heart".

    "Andy never took the easy musical route. His overdrive overdrove us into being the only funk/rock/punk band in the New Romantic movement, with songs that still survive, decades later.".

    Watch: Andy Taylor tells the BBC about his cancer diagnosis in 2023.

    Sir Rod, who wrote five songs with Taylor for the 1988 album Out of Order, recalled them making "some good music together" and having "some outrageous fun".

    Kemp said Taylor "influenced many of us along the way with his sparse staccato style", adding: "He brought shameless rock to the mix.".

    In a band tribute, Spandau Ballet called him "a hugely talented musician and an crucial part of the British music scene".

    US guitarist Nile Rodgers, the co-founder of Chic, recalled "countless great days and nights" with his "dear friend".

    Belinda Carlisle said she was "blessed" to have worked with Taylor, who played the guitar solo and was in the video for her song Mad About You.

    Former Led Zeppelin frontman Robert Plant called Taylor "a tough fighter", while Then Jerico's Mark Shaw remembered him as "one of the greatest musicians and songwriters I've ever heard and had the privilege to work with".

    Taylor (second left) married his wife Tracey at the Chateau Marmont hotel in Los Angeles in 1982.

    Taylor's wife Tracey, a hairstylist he met during the early days of Duran Duran, and whom he married in 1982, mentioned: "For all the incredible experiences music brought him, family always came first for Taylor, adding: "Nothing made him happier than having us all together.".

    She said he faced the last few years "with so much courage and determination" and said they were "grateful" for the "kindness and support shown to him by fans throughout his illness", saying it brought him "immense comfort and strength".

    Andy Taylor's guitar riffs powered some of Duran Duran's best-known songs.

    The son of a fisherman, Taylor taught himself guitar, bass, and drums and began playing professionally at age 13.

    He played with several bands around the UK before answering a music paper advertisement for a "live-wire guitarist", which led to his audition for Duran Duran in Birmingham in April 1980.

    The group went on to achieve global fame through the New Romantic movement, which combined slick, melodic synth-pop with aspirational music videos and chiselled good looks.

    Taylor's guitar lines - full of glassy, powerful riffs - were often a highlight of their songs, from the choppy opening of Girls on Film to the sleazy scuzz of Hungry Like The Wolf.

    Duran Duran bridged the sounds of pop, funk, disco, punk and newly introduced wave with a sound that remains indelibly tied to the 1980s.

    Duran Duran were one of the biggest pop acts of the 1980s, and its five members became global hearththrobs.

    Their indelible hooks and airbrushed music videos found a natural home on the newly rolled out MTV, giving their career a huge boost in the US.

    They became so popular in the US that the press labeled them the leaders of a "second British invasion" of the charts - alongside groups like Spandau Ballet, Human League and Eurythmics.

    During a hiatus in 1984, Andy and John Taylor enlisted Robert Palmer for their successful but short-lived side project the Power Station.

    The following year, the guitarist decided to quit Duran Duran after a miserable experience performing at Live Aid.

    "We'd reached rock bottom and we had absolutely nothing to say to each other," he wrote in his autobiography, Wild Boy.

    "We drove to the venue through streets packed with excited rock fans, but inside the bus the atmosphere was as if we were on a way to a funeral.".

    He went on to play on Palmer's Addicted To Love, and released a solo album, Thunder, in 1987.

    Taylor quit Duran Duran at the height of their fame in 1985, but rejoined the band several times in the 2000s and contributed to their most recent album, Danse Macabre.

    After a period writing and producing albums for other artists, he rejoined Duran Duran in 2000, lasting for just one album (2004's Astronaut) before parting ways again.

    In 2022, when the band were inducted to the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame, Taylor was notably absent from the ceremony, despite public plans for a reunion.

    When the group took the stage, Le Bon read a letter from the guitarist, in which he revealed his diagnosis with stage 4 metastatic prostate cancer.

    Nonetheless, he contributed to the following year's Halloween-themed album Danse Macabre, marking his final collaboration with the band.

    The following BBC programmes will pay tribute to Taylor:.

    Duran Duran at the BBC, on BBC Four on Friday 27 November at 21:30 GMT.

    Sounds of the 80s, on Radio 2 on Saturday 28 November at at 18:00 GMT.
